title: Log regular quotient after a tame equivariant modification
statement:
Let $C$ be an integral excellent separated Noetherian scheme, and let $B\subset C$ be a nowhere dense closed subset such that $(C,B)$ is a log regular pair. Let a finite group $G$ of order invertible on $C$ act on $C$, preserving $B$. Assume that the action is generically free, meaning free on geometric points over a $G$-stable dense open subset, and admissible, meaning every orbit lies in an affine open. Let $\pi:C\to X=C/G$ be the finite scheme quotient, with $X$ integral excellent Noetherian; the quotient has the orbit-space topology and structure sheaf $(\pi_*\mathcal O_C)^G$. There exist an integral excellent Noetherian scheme $M$, a proper birational morphism $\rho:M\to X$, and a nowhere dense closed subset $B_M\subset M$ such that $(M,B_M)$ is a log regular pair and $\rho^{-1}(\pi(B))\subseteq B_M$. Birational means inducing an isomorphism on dense open subschemes.

The notions are [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-trf-log-regular-pair], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Here separated means that the diagonal $C\to C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}C$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Expose VIII Theorem 1.1, printed p. 85, and Expose VI Proposition 3.2, printed p. 74; their quotient-modification consequence is written out in Expose IX 2.3--2.4, printed p. 134. Invertible group order implies tame inertia at every point.

proof.text: The stabilizer of a geometric point is a subgroup of $G$, so its order divides $|G|$ and is invertible: the action is tame. Apply [lem-per-gabber-equivariant-log-modification] to $C,B,G$ (its hypotheses are exactly those of the item, with excellence) to obtain $C_1$, the equivariant $f:C_1\to C$, a dense open $C^0\subseteq C$ with $f^{-1}(C^0)\to C^0$ an isomorphism, and $B_1=f^{-1}(B\cup T)$ with $(C_1,B_1)$ log regular and the action very tame. Over every affine open $W'\subseteq C$, $f^{-1}(W')\to W'$ is a closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^N_{W'}$ followed by projection. Put $V=\bigcap_{g\in G}gC^0\setminus(B\cup T)$. It is invariant; it is open and dense, since $C$ is irreducible, $B$ is nowhere dense, and $T$ is closed with $C\setminus T$ nonempty because the action is generically free. As $V\subseteq C^0$, the restriction $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ of the isomorphism over $C^0$ is an isomorphism, and $f^{-1}(V)$ is dense in $C_1$ by the last clause of the cited node.

source.place: VIII Theorem 1.1, p.85; IX Theorem 2.3, p.134

proof.text: For every affine open $W\subset X$, the finite morphism $\pi$ makes $C_W=\pi^{-1}W$ affine Noetherian. Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] with the identity projective morphism $W\to W$ and the finite map $C_W\to W$: this last map is H-projective. The projective morphism $C_{1,W}\to C_W$ followed by this map is H-projective by [lem-trf-h-projective-composition]. Apply [lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient] over the affine base $W$ to $C_{1,W}$. Obtain a finite surjective quotient $q_W:C_{1,W}\to M_W$ and a projective $M_W\to W$, with $M_W$ integral, geometric fibres equal to orbits, and invariant structure sheaf.

source.place: IX 2.4, quotient diagram, p.134; local finite projective quotient construction

proof.text: For affine inclusions $W'\subset W$, the open $C_{1,W'}$ is invariant. The restriction clause of [lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient] identifies its quotient with the open inverse image of $W'$ in $M_W$. Categorical uniqueness makes these identifications the identity on repeated restrictions and makes their composites equal for triples. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-glueing-affine-opens] to obtain $\rho:M\to X$ restricting to $M_W\to W$. The local maps $q_W$ agree under these identifications, so glue to $q:C_1\to M$. Every orbit is contained in some $C_{1,W}$ and, there, in an affine fibre-preimage of an affine open of $M_W$ under the finite map $q_W$; hence the action on $C_1$ is admissible. The glued quotient has orbit-space topology, geometric orbit fibres and invariant structure sheaf because all these descriptions restrict to the $W$.

Each $M_W\to W$ is projective, hence proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. Properness is local on the target by [lemma-nagata-projective-target-local], so $\rho$ is proper. It is locally of finite type by the definition of properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Each $M_W$ is integral; the images $q(f^{-1}V)$ meet all nonempty open sets of $M$, since their inverse images meet the dense open $f^{-1}V$ under the surjective quotient map. This image is irreducible, as the image of the irreducible scheme $V$. Thus $M$ is irreducible and locally reduced, hence integral. For a finite affine cover of the Noetherian scheme $X$, the finite-type local descriptions in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] give a finite affine cover of $M$ by finite-type algebras over excellent affine coordinate rings of $X$. Those algebras are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], and hence Noetherian. This proves excellence and Noetherianity of $M$.

Set $B_M=q(B_1)$. The hypotheses of [lem-per-very-tame-quotient-log-regular] now hold: $(C_1,B_1)$ is log regular, the action is generically free on $f^{-1}V$, it is very tame by Step 1, and admissibility and the finite quotient were established in Steps 2–3. The cited theorem gives the fs log regular pair $(M,B_M)$, including its dense open triviality locus. Thus $B_M$ is a nowhere dense closed subset.

source.place: VI Theorem 3.2 and Proposition 3.5(c), pp.74–75; IX 2.4, p.134

proof.text: The invariant dense open $V\subset C$ is saturated for $\pi$ because the fibres are orbits. Its image $O=\pi(V)$ is open by the quotient topology and dense because $\pi$ is surjective and $V$ is dense. The equality $\rho q=\pi f$ implies $q^{-1}(\rho^{-1}O)=f^{-1}V$. The equivariant isomorphism $f^{-1}V\simeq V$ identifies their orbit spaces and invariant sheaves, and therefore identifies $\rho^{-1}O\to O$ with an isomorphism of schemes. The source open is dense by Step 4. Hence $\rho$ is birational in the stated dense-open sense.

source.place: IX 2.4, p.134: the descended map is a modification

proof.text: Because $B$ is invariant and the fibres of $\pi$ are orbits, $\pi^{-1}(\pi(B))=B$. For $m\in\rho^{-1}(\pi(B))$, choose $c_1$ over $m$ under the surjective map $q$. Then $\pi(f(c_1))=\rho(m)\in\pi(B)$, so $f(c_1)\in B$ and $c_1\in f^{-1}B\subset B_1$. It follows that $m=q(c_1)\in q(B_1)=B_M$. This proves the required inclusion without adding or enlarging any boundary.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q70-854facfa9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read ILO VIII 1.1 and 1.2 (pp.85-86), VI 1.2-1.4 and 3.1-3.5 (pp.69-74), IX 2.2-2.4 (pp.133-134), Stacks 01W8 (excellent schemes) and 07QU, every cited node's statement, and both new nodes in full. Two repairable C3/C4 faults, both in the new node lem-per-gabber-equivariant-log-modification and both used in Step 1. (1) The node defined projective as a closed immersion into projective space 'Zariski locally on the target'. Step 1 asserts, and Step 2 needs, H-projectivity over every affine open of C, which a locally projective map over an affine need not have. The source's EGA-projective over a Noetherian base does give the per-affine form, so the node now states that. (2) 'An isomorphism between dense opens' does not give f^{-1}(V) ≅ V, which Step 1 asserts and Step 6 needs to get q^{-1}ρ^{-1}O = f^{-1}V. The full-preimage form follows because f is separated and C_1 is irreducible, so the node now states f^{-1}(C^0) ≅ C^0 for a dense open C^0. I also put the very-tame stalks on C_1, the scheme the condition is about. Step 1 is rewritten with V = ∩ gC^0 minus (B ∪ T); its uses are unchanged. Fixed files are under fixes/dag/nodes/sec-deligne-laumon-a1/. Steps 2-7 check out: C_W is affine; finite-over-projective with p = id; 01WE composition; Rydh quotient over B = W; 01LH gluing, with the cocycle from categorical uniqueness; admissibility from the finite q_W; properness from 01WC and 08J0; integrality as the image of irreducible C_1 with integral charts; excellence via a finite cover of X by excellent affines and 07QU, matching the Stacks cover definition; VI 3.2 hypotheses all checked; birationality from saturation of V; the boundary inclusion is elementary. The new VI 3.2 node matches 3.2, 3.5 and 1.4, and VIII 1.2(b) agrees with it. No duplicates: the X 1.1 trait node is relative and log-smooth, and the projective-quotient node has no log structure. No SGA citation.
